standard_prerequisites.name: The geometric case for a regular section, the definition of capping with a first Chern class, and the Gysin definition
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-geometric-cap (proof line 5154), together with Definition definition-cap-c1 (proof line 5163) and Definition definition-gysin-homomorphism (proof line 5165)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first computes the cap for components not contained in the divisor, and the two definitions identify the remaining terms with the Gysin pullback and its pushforward.

core_obligations: Split the cycle according to whether its components are contained in the divisor: for a component not contained in the divisor the cap with the first Chern class is the class of the intersection with the divisor, by the geometric case (proof lines 5147-5154).
Write the cap as the sum of those terms and the terms coming from the components contained in the divisor, using the definition of the cap (proof lines 5155-5163).

Observe that the result matches termwise the pushforward of the Gysin pullback given by the Gysin definition, which proves the statement and thus the particular case for an effective Cartier divisor (proof lines 5164-5166).
proof_roadmap: Components not contained in the divisor (proof lines 5147-5154).
Assembly of the cap from the definition (proof lines 5155-5163).
Termwise comparison with the Gysin pullback (proof lines 5164-5166).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the composite of the pushforward with the Gysin pullback along the zero scheme of a section equals the cap with the first Chern class of the invertible sheaf, with the special case for an effective Cartier divisor (statement lines 5137-5145, tag 02TQ-adjacent). The proof splits the cycle according to whether its components lie in the divisor, uses the geometric case for those which do not, assembles the cap from its definition, and compares termwise with the Gysin pullback. The splitting and the termwise comparison are the substance, so the claim is H2.
